stories.exam_facts: More than 80 per cent of global merchandise trade is carried by sea. The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply; before the disruption around 120 vessels crossed it daily, and by early March traffic measured by gross tonnage had fallen by approximately 95 per cent, UNCTAD said. Chattogram Port, which handles around 92 per cent of Bangladesh's external trade, handled 3.4 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of containers in 2025, up 4.07 per cent from 2024; total cargo throughput reached 820 million tonnes, up 11.43 per cent, and vessel calls rose 10.5 per cent to 4,273. The port ranked 68th among the world's top 100 container ports in Lloyd's List's 2025 assessment. Syed Aref Sarwar of Red Sea Gateway Terminal, operator of Patenga Container Terminal, said the terminal had yet to experience a slowdown. Dr M Masrur Reaz of Policy Exchange Bangladesh warned the disruptions and higher bunker fuel costs could fuel inflation at a time when price pressures were already elevated.

stories.exam_facts: Under the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017, a marriage involving a girl under the age of 18 or a boy under the age of 21 is considered child marriage, and the law provides for a maximum of two years' imprisonment for contracting, solemnising or conducting one. The Department of Women Affairs prevented 1,474 child marriages in 2024 and 968 in 2025, after 1,846 in 2023; figures for prevention after June 2026 have not yet been compiled. Calls to the National Emergency Service 999 reporting child marriage fell from 6,499 in 2023 to 4,109 in 2024 and 3,045 in 2025, from an average of five complaints a day three years ago. Prothom Alo spoke to a schoolgirl from Rangabali upazila in Patuakhali, president of a local adolescent club run by the Village Education Resource Centre (VERC) with support from Manusher Jonno Foundation, who was forced to marry three months before her Secondary School Certificate examination and was divorced within three months after her husband pressed her for a dowry. Laila Khondkar, convenor of Shishurai Shob, said people were treating child marriage as normal and giving up, believing it cannot be eliminated. Note: the collected body text was truncated after 'From January to August this', so the 2026 figure for 999 calls was not available to this writer.

stories.exam_facts: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (Bapex) says a 10th well, Bhola North-3, is now being tested for a further 20 to 25 million cubic feet a day. Nationally, demand is about 3,800 million cubic feet a day, while supply averaged about 2,650 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year up to April 2026, according to the energy minister. Intraco Refueling Station signed a 10-year agreement with the state-owned Sundarban Gas Company in May 2023, with supply to industries around Dhaka beginning that December; the contract calls for 5 million cubic feet a day, rising to 25 million, but Intraco was carrying only about 3.5 million before its supply was largely suspended from November 2025 over safety licensing of its trailers, resuming fully in August 2026 after the Department of Explosives cleared them. By ferry, the cost for a single pickup truck is about Tk15,000, while carrying gas by road can cost up to almost Tk20,000, and drivers say a Dhaka-Bhola trip that took around 10 to 11 hours by road can now be done in about six to seven hours by vessel. The Carnival Wave's wide deck can hold up to 40 private cars, or 20 to 25 larger vehicles such as trucks, and its sister ferry is the MV Carnival Cruise.

The editorial says the tasks ahead include dealing with the legacy of Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) and replenishing the capital of banks whose losses have eaten into their capital base, and it reports the central bank's optimism about making significant progress in addressing the NPL issue by December this year, while noting the public would like to know how much of such loans could actually be recovered rather than rescheduled. The final stage's measures include better protection of deposits, more rigorous scrutiny of borrowers' creditworthiness and gradual phasing out of emergency support, and the editorial argues the banking regulator itself needs the freedom to enforce discipline in lending irrespective of changes in the government's policy stance, given the history of bank loans concentrated in a few business groups.
